nutshell: Nasdaq falls, Dow rises on mixed corporate earnings

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the February 4th closing bell briefing. The market showed a major divergence across the indices today.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today can be summed up in one phrase: mixed corporate earnings sent the Nasdaq down and the Dow up. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained over 0.5% to close at 49,501, but the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell sharply by more than 1.5% to finish at 22,904. The S&P 500 also slipped 0.5%. While private employment data released early in the session came in weaker than expected, the market's attention was squarely focused on the fourth-quarter report cards of individual companies.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the split fortunes of the indices were really driven by earnings reports. The drop in tech stocks looks particularly steep.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. A prime example is the semiconductor company AMD. Despite reporting Q4 results that beat estimates, its stock plunged over 17% after it issued a future revenue forecast that fell short of market expectations. This kind of concern about future growth sparked a sell-off across the entire Nasdaq. On the flip side, pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly surged more than 10% after delivering strong earnings and an optimistic outlook, which led a rally in healthcare stocks and helped lift the Dow. Ultimately, it was a day where the market showed strict differentiation based on the fundamentals of individual companies.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it was a day where the market reacted sharply to the details of earnings and future guidance. Could you break down the key themes that moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, I'll focus on two main points: first, the diverging paths of tech and value stocks due to those mixed earnings, and second, how strength in healthcare and industrials allowed the Dow to rally on its own. We'll look at each of these in detail.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with that divergence between tech and value stocks. The key takeaway today was that the market reacted more sensitively to future outlooks than to the actual earnings numbers, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. You could say the market was completely split in two today. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained over 0.5%, showing a solid performance, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell more than 1.5%, a stark contrast. Behind this decoupling were investors' differing views on companies' future growth prospects. The tech sector ETF, XLK, dropped nearly 2%, while the healthcare sector ETF, XLV, and the industrials ETF, XLI, both finished higher, clearly illustrating the split. The ISM Services PMI, which came in stronger than expected at 53.8, reinforced the idea that the service-oriented real economy is still robust, which was a positive for traditional value stocks. On the other hand, despite weak private jobs data, the 10-year Treasury yield rose slightly, adding pressure on growth stocks like those in the tech sector.

sources.title: ism services pmi

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: And at the center of the tech sell-off was AMD. Can you break down exactly why the stock fell so hard despite reporting good earnings?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right, AMD actually posted solid Q4 results, with both revenue and earnings per share beating market estimates. But the stock still plunged over 10%, and the problem was its guidance for the next quarter. The company's Q1 revenue forecast raised concerns that it wouldn't meet the market's high expectations. This also implies that after the stock surged over 90% in the past year on the AI boom, investors were expecting near-perfect growth. This disappointment weighed not only on AMD but also on other AI-related stocks like NVIDIA, dampening investor sentiment across the tech sector. It's a case that shows strong current earnings alone can't guarantee a stock's rise; if a company can't provide confidence in its future growth path, profit-taking can emerge at any time.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: In complete contrast to AMD, the Dow showed strong gains, led by pharmaceutical stocks.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's correct. The main driver behind the Dow's rise was the pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly. Along with Q4 earnings that beat expectations, Eli Lilly provided a 2026 annual profit forecast that was well above Wall Street's estimates, fueled by soaring demand for its weight-loss drugs. By showing such strong confidence in its future growth, the stock jumped over 10%, with its market cap even surpassing $950 billion. This strength in pharma and biotech lifted the entire healthcare sector. On top of that, other Dow components like GE HealthCare also issued positive earnings outlooks, supporting the index's rise. It was a clear example of a market rotation, with investors who were nervous about tech stocks moving into value stocks that demonstrated solid earnings and growth drivers.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, today's market can be summed up as a tight tug-of-war between growth and value stocks. Do you think this trend will continue?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It's too early to say for sure, but it's definitely a key theme running through this earnings season. Tech stocks, which have rallied on the massive expectations around AI, are now on the hot seat to prove those expectations with actual numbers. Meanwhile, traditional value stocks that generate steady profits based on a solid real economy are emerging as a relatively attractive safe haven. The fact that AI startup Anthropic unveiled a new tool that could threaten the existing software industry has also increased caution around the tech sector, fueling this rotation. Therefore, for the time being, the market is expected to show even greater differentiation by sector and stock, depending on the future guidance individual companies provide.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, and in that environment of differentiation, the Dow's solo rally was particularly striking. What was the driving force that lifted the Dow even as tech stocks struggled?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, today marked a clear shift in the market's center of gravity from growth to value stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.53% to close as the only gainer, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell over 1.5% and the S&P 500 was down about 0.5%. This decoupling was driven by mixed economic data and corporate earnings. The ADP private employment report came in well below expectations, raising concerns of an economic slowdown, but soon after, the ISM Services PMI showed expansion beyond forecasts, confirming the resilience of the U.S. economy. Amid these conflicting signals, the 10-year Treasury yield remained relatively stable, and investors focused more on individual company earnings and fundamentals rather than the macroeconomic direction, moving capital into the healthcare and industrials sectors.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: You mentioned the healthcare sector, and specifically Eli Lilly, was at the heart of the Dow's rally. How good were its earnings, exactly?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Well, Eli Lilly posted quarterly earnings that beat market expectations and issued a very strong annual forecast, causing its stock to surge over 10% in a single day. The explosive sales growth of its weight-loss and diabetes drugs was the main driver of its performance. Lilly's success created a tailwind for the entire healthcare sector. GE HealthCare also posted solid results and rose nearly 5%. As a result, the healthcare sector ETF, XLV, gained over 1.2% today, acting as the biggest shield against downward market pressure. With tech stocks undergoing a correction, investors flocked to companies that could prove they have reliable profit growth.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Along with healthcare, you also mentioned the industrials sector was strong. What was the story there?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The strength in industrials goes hand-in-hand with that ISM services data I mentioned earlier. The fact that the services sector is stronger than expected can be interpreted as a sign that the U.S. economy is still holding up firmly. This raises expectations that the earnings of industrial companies, which are sensitive to the economic cycle, will remain stable going forward. Indeed, the industrials sector ETF, XLI, closed slightly higher, contrasting with the weakness in tech. When market uncertainty increases, investors tend to seek stability in traditional blue-chip stocks that generate steady profits now, like those in the industrial sector that form the backbone of the economy, rather than in growth stocks selling a future dream. Today was exactly that kind of day.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, in the end, traditional value stocks, backed by solid earnings and economic stability, were the stars of the show today. Could you give us a final summary?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that's right. Today's market can be summed up as 'strict differentiation and rotation based on earnings.' Companies like Eli Lilly, which demonstrated overwhelming earnings and growth potential, surged regardless of the broader index moves. Conversely, companies like AMD, which raised concerns about their future outlook, fell sharply. In this process, we saw a clear flow of capital moving out of the tech sector, which had been leading the market, and into value sectors like healthcare and industrials. This is analyzed as a significant shift, suggesting that after the early-year rally, the market is raising its standards and scrutinizing growth stocks with high valuation burdens more carefully, while seeking new investment opportunities in value stocks with solid profits.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, as you said, it was a day of extreme differentiation between stocks based on their earnings. Let's focus on AMD, which really illustrates this trend. The earnings were good, yet the stock plunged over 17%. What on earth happened?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, it was a classic case of just how difficult it is to meet sky-high market expectations. On paper, AMD's results were excellent. Its 2025 annual revenue increased by 34% year-over-year, and notably, revenue from its key growth driver, the data center segment, grew by 32%, proving that demand for AI chips is strong. Even the company's Q1 2026 revenue forecast was above Wall Street's average estimate. The stock plunged nonetheless because of disappointment that the results didn't meet the market's enormous expectations that had driven the stock up, and because underlying risks that had been simmering below the surface came into focus. It seems the market wanted more than perfection.

sources.title: AMD's Stock Takes a Hit Despite Solid Earnings. What Happened?

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: It seems hard to explain a nearly 17% drop with just disappointment over guidance. You mentioned underlying risks came to the surface, which seems more significant. What specific risk factors are being discussed?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that was the core driver of today's decline. There are two major structural risks being highlighted. First is the supply chain risk, as the company relies entirely on a single source, Taiwan's TSMC, for the production of its most advanced chips. This implies that if geopolitical tensions in the Taiwan Strait escalate, AMD's entire core product line could grind to a halt. Second is its high dependency on the Chinese market. In fiscal year 2025, 22.4% of its total revenue came from China, which is seen as highly unstable revenue that could evaporate at any moment due to tightening U.S. export controls on semiconductors to China. In fact, there's a precedent where restrictions on the export of specific AI accelerators led to hundreds of millions of dollars in inventory-related costs, which has heightened investor concerns.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Supply chain and dependency on a single market—those are definitely risks you can't ignore. But despite these risks, aren't there still those who see high growth potential for AMD? What are they focusing on?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Those who remain positive despite the risks believe a 'game-changer' has emerged that can offset all these concerns: the massive partnership with OpenAI. In a recent filing, AMD announced a multi-year strategic partnership to supply OpenAI with 6 gigawatts of GPUs. This is more than just securing a large customer; it's a symbolic event that validates their top-tier technology and cracks NVIDIA's monopoly in the AI accelerator market. Analysis suggests this one deal alone could generate billions of dollars in stable revenue over the next few years, overwhelming the uncertainty related to China sales. On top of that, its leadership position in the emerging AI PC market is also cited as a powerful growth driver.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it's a tug-of-war between a clear growth driver in OpenAI and the geopolitical risks of TSMC and China. Should we interpret today's market reaction as giving more weight to the risks?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's an excellent point. Today's stock movement shows the market reacted more sensitively to the immediate risks than to the growth potential. In conclusion, the assessment of AMD is sharply divided. On one side, some believe that based on strong fundamentals and the definite growth engine of the OpenAI deal, the current stock drop is an opportunity created by irrational fear. On the other side, some warn that uncontrollable external variables like TSMC and China are critical risks that could threaten the company's very existence. Therefore, the future direction of the stock will likely be determined by how the market judges whether this grand growth narrative can overcome the geopolitical risks.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: The market closed with a somewhat confusing picture today. Could you briefly recap the day's action?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, the market struggled to find direction today after a stronger-than-expected ISM Services PMI report was released. While the data showed the U.S. economy remains robust, it was also interpreted as a signal that the Fed has no reason to rush into rate cuts, which pressured investor sentiment. In the end, the major indices were mixed, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq falling and the Dow rising slightly. It was a day where optimism about an economic soft landing and concerns about a prolonged period of high interest rates were in a tense standoff.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So what should we be watching for in tomorrow's market?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Tomorrow, we'll get some important data that will help gauge the heat of the labor market. First, we have the weekly initial jobless claims, where the market expects a slight increase to 212,000 from the previous figure of 209,000. If this number comes in lower than expected, it means layoffs are still low, providing evidence of a strong job market. We also need to watch the JOLTS report, which shows job openings. The market is currently forecasting a slight increase to 7.2 million job openings, and since this acts as a leading indicator of labor demand, investors could react sensitively to it.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So tomorrow's jobs data will serve as a preview for the even bigger events coming next week.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. All eyes are ultimately on next week. That's when the two most important reports that will set the market's direction will be released back-to-back: the January Jobs Report and the Consumer Price Index, or CPI. The non-farm payrolls number, out on the 11th, is expected to show an increase of 68,000, a slight improvement from last month's 50,000. The inflation rate, to be released on the 13th, is forecast to have risen 0.1% month-over-month, a slowdown from the previous reading. If these two indicators show what's expected—stable employment while inflation is being contained—the market could see a relief rally. Conversely, if either one deviates from market expectations, we could see significant volatility.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Finally, what's your closing thought for investors?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right now, we're in a 'data-dependent' market, where every economic report is being examined under a microscope to predict the Fed's next move. Especially with the major hurdles of employment and inflation data to clear next week, it's important to try to read the broader trend in the data rather than reacting emotionally to short-term volatility. The market's interpretation can change by the minute before and after these reports are released, so this is a time when it's wise to calmly observe the market's reaction and respond accordingly, rather than engaging in hasty buying or panic selling.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, thank you again for your valuable insights. That concludes our February 4th closing bell briefing. Thanks for listening.
